page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core). It is configured with 128 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-dense 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The processor architecture includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for vector workloads via AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 instruction sets.

Benchmark results place the system consistently in the top tier for compute and memory throughput. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 233,270.61 and a single-core score of 3,787.98, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 116,710.13. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 410.03 GB/sec for reads and 205.23 GB/sec for writes. The platform also yields top-tier throughput in network-adjacent and runtime services, generating 171.03 million Redis SET operations per second and 103.82 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. CPU-based machine learning inference is robust for smaller parameters, reaching 5,809.53 tokens per second on prompt processing for a 135M model and 316.09 tokens per second for a 7B model, though large 70B parameter text generation decreases to an average 5.06 tokens per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the constrained memory ratio of 2 GB per core and the lack of bundled local storage. Because no local NVMe drives are provisioned, workloads requiring disk access rely entirely on remote storage volumes. Cost efficiency is maximized in compute-bound environments where high single-thread clock speeds, complete core dedication, and vector math instructions dominate, avoiding expenditure on unused RAM.

Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is tailored for high-performance computing, batch data processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, continuous integration pipelines, video encoding, and distributed web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 64 dedicated cores alongside 128 GB of RAM (2 GB per vCPU). The underlying AMD architecture features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits top-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, achieving 233,270.61 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 171.03 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance contains no bundled local disk storage, necessitating remote premium storage attachments. With its low memory-to-core footprint and dense compute profile, the F64als_v7 provides strong cost efficiency for high-performance compute tasks, code compilation, video transcoding, and web server fleets.
